title: Developer Relations Engineer
description:
At Nextcloud we help our users achieve a safe home for all their data, secure, under your control, and developed in an open, transparent, and trustworthy way. We work remotely, and our work culture is shaped by mutual trust, enthusiasm, and a strong belief in the principles of open source.

We're looking for an engineer who has built Nextcloud apps to join our Developer Relations Team and help grow the Nextcloud app ecosystem!

Responsibilities

  • Growing the number of apps in the Nextcloud App Store.

  • Creating and improving educational materials for app developers (tutorials, courses, documentation).

  • Reviewing apps from commercial app development partners and supporting them.

  • Onboarding commercial app development partners to ensure a successful product offering and customer support.

  • Representing Nextcloud by giving talks and workshops at open-source conferences around the world. Regular travel is required.

  • Testing and reviewing community apps for release highlights.

  • Contributing to technical customer support as part of the Engineering department.

Requirements

  • Proven experience developing Nextcloud apps (add a link to your code in your application).

  • Technical experience with PHP or Python (both is a plus).

  • The following experience is a plus: a bit of HTML, CSS, JavaScript, one or more frontend frameworks such as VueJS, React, Angular, or Svelte, and understanding of containerization (Docker).

  • Strong written and spoken English; comfortable teaching, presenting and writing documentation.

  • Experience with public speaking (if available, add links to recordings of your talks in your application).

  • Knowledge about open source technology and communities (experience in Developer Relations or a track record of contributing to other open source projects is a plus).

  • Ability to prioritise and work effectively within time constraints.

  • Reliability and an independent, self-reliant working style.

What we offer

  • A distributed, open team with a passion for working on and within the open source community.

  • Developing a product which pushes the boundaries of technology with a global user and contributor community.

  • A competitive salary.

  • Flexibility for a healthy work-life balance.

  • Time for personal growth and education.

If you are interested in this role, please submit your application along with your resume and a link to a Nextcloud app you developed.

An overview of this role

We are looking for a Backend Engineer to join our Change Record team within GitLab’s Source Code stage. As AI agents increasingly write code alongside people, every change needs a clear, trustworthy record of what changed, why, and who or what made it. You’ll build that record into GitLab’s source code experience, for humans and agents alike. That work happens in one of GitLab’s oldest and most complex product areas, where you’ll use Ruby on Rails to improve a critical system serving GitLab.com, self-managed instances, and GitLab Dedicated.   • Experience writing backend unit and integration tests, with familiarity with the testing pyramid, Git, and collaborative code review processes.

The functional team works across Europe and North America, supporting both synchronous and asynchronous collaboration. It includes four engineers, comprising both backend and frontend engineers. title: Manager, Deployment Lead, Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) - Singapore
description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) team partners with customers to turn research breakthroughs into production systems. We operate at the intersection of customer delivery and core platform development.

About the Role

As a Manager of our Deployment Leads in APAC, you’ll lead and grow a team of DLs through high-stakes customer deployments, owning technical and business outcomes end to end. You’ll help build the function as you lead it, navigating significant ambiguity to define its scope and ways of working.

You’ll partner with FDE, Product, Research, and GTM to balance customer-specific solutions with reusable capabilities and ensure field insights inform product priorities. Drawing on your experience leading complex technical deployments and products, you’ll guide decisions on scope, feasibility, sequencing, and delivery readiness, helping your team make sound tradeoffs and build lasting customer trust.

Success will be measured by the impact of your team’s deployments, the growth of your DLs, and how effectively the team and delivery model scale.

This role is based in Singapore. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. This role will require travel up to 25%.

In this role, you will:

  • Lead and grow a team of DLs delivering production systems with frontier models

  • Own end-to-end delivery outcomes, from scoping through production, adoption, and handoff

  • Set direction and build trust across technical teams, GTM, and customer executives

  • Codify what works into practical playbooks, consistent delivery practices, and product roadmap inputs

  • Set a high bar for DL performance through hands-on coaching, actionable feedback, and career development

  • Make staffing decisions, develop future DL leaders, and build a team that scales without unnecessary complexity

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Bring 8+ years of customer-facing technical delivery or product leadership experience, including 2+ years managing high-performing teams.

  • Have personally led complex technical deployments from prototype through production, adoption, and handoff.

  • Have a strong product mindset, ideally with product management experience, and can balance customer-specific needs with reusable solutions.

  • Thrive in ambiguity and enjoy building new functions: creating structure where little exists, making sound decisions with incomplete information, and adapting as priorities evolve.

  • Build deep trust across technical teams, Product, Research, GTM, and customer leadership.

description:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

*Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role

As a Staff Software Engineer on GitLab's Authentication team, you'll be the technical lead for how every user, application, token, and automated agent proves who it is on GitLab.com, Self-Managed, and Dedicated.

We're an OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect (OIDC) provider for millions of users. We also accept identity from enterprise identity providers through Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) and Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP). Behind that sit more than ten token types and several session methods that grew inside the Ruby on Rails monolith. You'll help us move this work onto GATE, GitLab's new authentication and authorization platform. GATE exchanges external credentials for short-lived tokens at the edge through a Secure Token Service written in Go.You'll set our technical direction, lead the hardest protocol and migration work yourself, and help senior engineers own the rest.

Our projects include:

  • OAuth across Cells: Making OAuth clients, grants, and tokens work when users and organizations live in different cells
  • Global identities: One user identity that works across organizations and cells
  • Token consolidation: Reducing the number of token types and moving token issuance and validation out of the monolith
  • Identity for artificial intelligence (AI) agents and workloads: OAuth for Model Context Protocol (MCP) clients, workload identity federation, and service identities with narrow scopes

What you'll do

  • Own the technical direction for authentication protocols at GitLab, including OAuth 2.0, OIDC, SAML, and token exchange, across the Rails monolith and GATE services.
  • Write and drive design documents and architecture decision records (ADRs) for multi-quarter work, then break that work into increments that ship behind feature flags.
  • Lead migrations that must not break existing customers: token formats, client and grant state, and session behavior on GitLab.com, Self-Managed, and Dedicated.
  • Be hands-on in the most complex parts of the code, in Ruby on Rails and Go, and review the designs and merge requests of other engineers.
  • Agree interface contracts with the GATE Core, GATE Infra, Authorization, and Tenant Scale (Cells and Organizations) teams, and keep them current as the architecture changes.
  • Treat authentication as a security and availability boundary: threat-model new flows, add rate limits and abuse controls, and lead the technical response to authentication incidents.
  • Mentor senior and intermediate engineers on the team and raise the protocol and security knowledge of the whole group.
  • Work asynchronously with engineers in India, Europe, and the Americas, with most decisions made in writing.
  • Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.

What you'll bring

  • Significant experience building and running production authentication or identity systems at scale, with technical leadership across teams that moves unclear problems to written decisions and shipped code.
  • Deep, hands-on knowledge of OAuth 2.0 and OIDC: authorization code with Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE), refresh token rotation, token exchange, client registration, scopes, and JSON Web Tokens (JWTs) with signing keys and key rotation.

Within Online Data, the Storage Foundationteam owns the online serving stores and databases that power Airbnb. We build and operate Airbnb's source-of-truth database: an open-source, distributed NewSQL system running on stateful Kubernetes. It stores critical data — users, listings, and more — and handles over half of all of Airbnb's online OLTP traffic. Our charter: keep this database reliable, secure, scalable, fast, correct, well-tested, and cost-efficient — at Airbnb's scale.

The Community You Will Join

We're hiring two roles within the Database team. Both are described below.

  • Database Performance & Reliability: Dig into the internals of a large-scale, multi-tenant, distributed database — storage, query execution, consensus, change data capture, and shard routing and management. You'll root-cause hard performance, reliability, and stability issues, and partner directly with our open-source database vendor to land fixes upstream.
  • Database Quality & Automation: Build the testing and quality infrastructure that lets us move fast with confidence on an open-source database. You'll bring tools like Jepsen and other database benchmarks into Airbnb's in-house testing stack, drive CI integration with OSS test suites, and design creative solutions for database tiering and representative load shadowing. As AI accelerates development speed and our availability bar climbs toward 99.99%, this role becomes only more critical to how fast and safely we can ship.

  • Build the frameworks and tooling around monitoring, observability, permissions, and service discovery integration.
  • Dig into the query and storage layers to explain latency differences between B-tree and LSM-based storage engines.
  • Design and implement traffic prioritization at the storage layer for connection pooling, CPU prioritization, and reason about traffic
  • Test, validate and safely roll out a new CDC architecture while guaranteeing full transactional correctness across shards.

Your Expertise

  • 5+ years building and operating large-scale, Tier 0 distributed systems.
  • Hands-on experience with database or storage internals: query execution, storage engines, replication, consensus and testing.
  • Ability to own and dive deeply into a complex codebase, ideally an open-source one.

title: Senior Systems Engineer, Tech Foundations
description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

The Community You Will Join:

The world is changing how it works; not just in where we do it, but in how fast and how well we can do it. Airbnb has already shown that we can move with speed and intention. We navigated a pandemic, rebuilt our company from the ground up, had a successful IPO, and shipped product upgrades – all while working remotely. That experience didn't just change where we work. It changed what we believe is possible.

Now, a new shift is underway. AI is fundamentally changing the leverage available to every team – compressing timelines, breaking down traditional job description silos, raising the ceiling on quality, and enabling small, focused groups to accomplish what once required much larger ones. At Airbnb, we are not treating AI as a future consideration. We are moving fast to embed it into how we operate today – using it to multiply the impact of every employee, every system, and decisions we make every day. The companies and teams that embrace this shift with urgency and discipline will define what's possible in the years ahead. We intend to be one of them.

Collaboration Products

The Collaboration Products team owns the enterprise systems that Airbnb's workforce relies on to plan, build, and deliver — including our Atlassian ecosystem, AI-powered tooling integrations, and custom-built engineering platforms. Our mission goes beyond keeping the lights on. We are moving fast to modernize our stack, retire technical debt, and integrate AI capabilities that directly multiply the productivity and quality of the teams we serve. We build with urgency, operate with rigor, and treat every system we touch as an opportunity to raise the bar on what BizTech delivers to Airbnb.

The Difference You Will Make:

The Senior Systems Engineer is a hands-on technical leader who moves fast, builds to last, and uses AI as a force multiplier — not a future initiative. In this role, you will own the configuration, migration, and continuous improvement of Airbnb's Atlassian platforms, including leading the active deprecation of Jira Data Center and full transition to Jira Cloud. But your impact goes beyond administration. You will identify where AI and automation can compress delivery cycles, reduce toil, and improve the quality and reliability of the systems our workforce depends on — and then build those improvements, quickly. You bring the platform depth to architect scalable solutions and the judgment to know when to move fast and when to be deliberate. You are the kind of engineer who raises the velocity and quality of everyone around you.

A Typical Day:

  • Serve as the primary SME and hands-on administrator for JiraCloud Software, JiraCloud Service Management (JSM), and associated Atlassian tooling; own configuration standards, governance, and technical debt reduction across the environment
  • Architect and implement scalable Jira configurations including custom workflows, issue type hierarchies, permission schemes, notification schemes, screens, and field configurations aligned with Atlassian best practices
  • Lead and execute Jira migrations - including Data Center to Cloud - coordinating with cross-functional stakeholders to deliver seamless cutover experiences
  • Design and configure Jira Service Management projects including SLAs, custom queues, JSM Forms, approval workflows, and security schemes to support internal service delivery teams
  • Build and maintain advanced analytics, dashboards, and reporting solutions using native tooling for Jira Cloud as a first line of options; Airbnb has elected to avoid Atlassian Marketplace products for information security, privacy & legal prerogatives. Airbnb is building custom Forge applications that will require your ongoing maintenance and partnership with supporting systems engineering teams.
  • Configure and administer Atlassian access management, user lifecycle management, license tier optimization, and security posture improvements
  • Evaluate if Atlassian Marketplace plugins architecture evolves to a point where Airbnb could consider adopting plugins where business needs dictate, and where security, legal, and privacy requirements are satisfied.
  • Act as a strategic partner to business stakeholders by leading requirements-gathering sessions, translating business needs into technical designs, and proactively identifying opportunities for automation and process improvement
  • Configure and expand Atlassian Rovo AI agents and automation rules; evaluate emerging AI/ML capabilities within the Atlassian ecosystem and champion responsible, contextually appropriate AI adoption aligned with Airbnb's mission
  • Write and maintain custom automation rules using Jira's native Automation engine and JavaScript; leverage Jira REST API for integrations, data imports, and custom reporting
  • Lead User Acceptance Testing (UAT) efforts for platform changes and migrations; develop and maintain test plans, test scripts, and defect tracking documentation
  • Facilitate Agile ceremonies (sprint planning, retrospectives, standups) as needed; operate as Scrum Master or Product Owner for platform-focused workstreams
  • Document system configurations, runbooks, and knowledge base articles to support operational continuity and enable self-service across the organization
  • Participate in on-call rotation and provide escalation support for critical Atlassian platform issues


Your Expertise:

  • 7+ years of hands-on Atlassian administration experience, including Jira Software, Jira Service Management (across JiraCloud & JiraDC) in enterprise environments with large user populations
  • Deep expertise in Jira workflow design, including post functions, validators, conditions, and custom properties; strong command of JQL for filters, subscriptions, dashboards, and board configuration
  • Proven experience leading Jira migrations (Data Center to Cloud), including project configuration migration, macro compatibility, and data integrity validation
  • Experience configuring and administering Jira Cloud native tooling for capacity planning and portfolio reporting
  • Proficiency with Atlassian Marketplace plugins including JavaScripting
  • Hands-on experience with Jira REST API using tools like Postman (GET/PUT/POST) for data extraction, integration, and custom reporting workflows
  • Experience integrating Atlassian tools with identity providers via LDAP & Okta; familiarity with user lifecycle management, license governance, and security hardening practices
  • Working knowledge of Atlassian Rovo and AI/ML capabilities within the Atlassian ecosystem; ability to configure Rovo agents with careful consideration for AI ethics, value alignment, and contextual appropriateness
  • Experience configuring Jira Automation rules (native and scripting-based); working knowledge of JavaScripting and JSON for custom automation
  • Strong background in Jira Service Management including SLA configuration, JSM Forms, custom queues, and approval workflows
  • Experience leading UAT for complex migrations and platform changes; proficiency in developing and executing test plans, test scripts, and defect documentation
  • Familiarity with SAFe Agile (SAFe Agilist and/or SAFe Scrum Master certification a plus); experience as Scrum Master or Product Owner for technical workstreams
  • Strong analytical and communication skills with a demonstrated ability to translate complex technical concepts for both technical and non-technical stakeholders
  • Experience working in a remote-first, high-growth environment; ability to independently manage multiple priorities and keep stakeholders informed
  • Familiarity with complementary enterprise tools such as Slack, Asana, Figma, Airtable, and Miro is an advantage

title: Staff Software Engineer, Streaming Infrastructure
description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

The Community You Will Join

Airbnb’s Data Infrastructure organization builds the platforms that power data across the company. Within it, the Data Movement & Transformation (DMT) pillar builds the platform that moves data between Airbnb’s storage engines and transforms it along the way.

Today, data moves through many bespoke, one-off pipelines that are built and maintained differently by each team. We’re replacing them with one unified, declarative platform. You define data once, and it is replicated everywhere it needs to go. This work underpins Airbnb’s Data as a Service initiative.

You’ll join the team that owns three connected layers of that platform:

  • Control plane: the layer that turns declarative data definitions into running pipelines, including provisioning, runtime selection, and lifecycle management.
  • Schema: how schemas are defined, tracked, and evolved safely across every system and engine.
  • Realtime Data Infrastructure (RTDI): Kafka and the streaming transport layer that real-time data flows through at scale.

As a Staff Software Engineer, you’ll set technical direction across these layers and stay hands-on in the code.

Examples of the Difference You’ll Make

  • Design and evolve the control plane that automatically provisions Kafka topics, registers schemas, and deploys pipelines from a declarative definition.
  • Build schema management that makes evolution safe and backward compatible across streaming, storage, and warehouse systems.
  • Improve the reliability, scalability, and cost efficiency of RTDI and Kafka at Airbnb’s scale, including capacity, multi-tenancy, and failure handling.
  • Replace fragmented pipeline tooling with shared, self-serve platform abstractions that other teams adopt.
  • Lead design reviews and incident follow-through, and raise the engineering and operational bar for the team.

Your Expertise

  • 9+ years of software engineering, including significant experience building and operating large-scale distributed systems, ideally data platforms, event-driven systems, or streaming infrastructure.
  • Hands-on experience with Kafka or a similar distributed log or messaging system, with a good understanding of partitioning, delivery semantics, throughput, and operational tradeoffs.
  • Experience designing schema or data contract systems, such as schema registries, serialization formats like Avro or Protobuf, and compatibility and evolution strategies.
  • Experience building control planes or platform APIs, such as declarative configuration, reconciliation, workflow orchestration, or resource provisioning, ideally on Kubernetes.
  • Familiarity with stream processing (e.g., Flink) or change data capture is a plus.
  • A track record of leading ambiguous, multi-quarter projects, taking them from design through delivery in production.
  • Ability to set technical direction, write clear design docs, and align multiple teams, and to mentor and grow other engineers.
  • Experience running large-scale systems in production, including on-call, incident response, and root cause analysis.
  • Writes clean, testable, maintainable code.
  • Strong collaboration and communication skills in a remote working environment.

description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

About the Team

The Talent Systems team within BizTech is the trusted technology partner to Employee Experience, Recruiting, Payroll, Procurement, Legal, and Privacy teams across Airbnb’s global operations. Driven by the philosophy of “High Tech, Human Touch,” we design and implement technology that meets both business objectives and employee needs: building robust frameworks that support the full employee journey, delivering AI-enabled self-service tools, and playing a key role in payroll management and benefits enrollment.

We own and operate a portfolio of 300+ production integrations and custom applications spanning payroll processors, benefits carriers, identity providers, compliance vendors, and internal platforms, with Workday at the center. We are also building the agentic layer on top of that portfolio: an Airbnb-owned Workday MCP server and AI assistant plugins that let employees and managers act on HR data directly from the tools they already use. You will partner closely with our Systems Architect, HR Centers of Excellence, IT Security, Finance, and external vendors to deliver enterprise-grade integrations and AI-enabled tooling that power Airbnb’s global HR technology ecosystem.

The Difference You Will Make

As a Staff Workday Integration Engineer, you are the technical authority for the integration initiatives that BizTech and Airbnb depend on. You will define our integration strategy and technical roadmap, set the architectural standards other engineers build against, and own the engineering of the Workday MCP and agentic integrations that are reshaping how employees interact with HR processes.

This is a hands-on builder role. You will personally write integration logic, own production reliability, and make the architectural decisions that keep HR data flowing correctly across our global employee population. You will drive touchless automation, reduce manual intervention, and ensure compliance across multiple jurisdictions. Your work directly impacts how thousands of Airbnb employees experience their payroll, benefits, time tracking, and HR processes.

You work alongside a Systems Architect who owns Talent Systems business process architecture, functional design, and the capability roadmap. You need enough functional fluency to build integrations and AI tools that are correct, and the engineering depth to make them reliable. As a Staff-level engineer, you will think 12+ months ahead, proactively surface systemic gaps, mentor the engineers around you, and establish patterns adopted across the Talent Systems team.

What You’ll Own

Integration Architecture & Technical Strategy

  • Define and own Airbnb’s Workday integration architecture standards, patterns, and governance frameworks
  • Lead architectural decisions for complex, high-risk integration initiatives, including global rollouts, payroll runs, benefits open enrollment, and system migrations
  • Evaluate and advise on build-vs-buy decisions, Workday-native-vs-middleware trade-offs, and long-term integration platform strategy
  • Establish reusable integration design patterns, error handling and retry frameworks, and observability standards adopted team-wide
  • Anticipate platform evolution and architect integrations that accommodate Workday’s semi-annual releases with minimal rework
  • Identify and remediate technical debt across the integration landscape: functionality, performance, error handling, and scalability

Core Workday Integration Development

  • Architect, design, build, and maintain complex inbound and outbound integrations using Workday Studio, Core Connectors, EIBs, Document Transforms, and RaaS API endpoints
  • Develop integrations against Workday Web Services (WWS): WSDL interpretation, web service versioning, request/response handling for SOAP and REST
  • Own design and delivery of high-volume integration scenarios: payroll runs, benefits open enrollment, global workforce changes, and multi-country rollouts
  • Own Workday payroll interfaces (PECI, PICOF) and their interaction with third-party payroll providers
  • Build and maintain advanced Custom Reports and Calculated Fields for integration and AI-tool consumption
  • Work within the Business Process Framework, understanding how process events trigger integration flows
  • Build and maintain Workday Extend applications (data models, business logic, UI pages, Extend REST APIs) when Extend is the right tool versus Studio, EIB, or middleware; Extend adoption strategy and SME ownership sit with the Systems Architect
  • Apply Workday Orchestrate for multi-system workflow coordination where it fits
  • Manage the integration portfolio across Workday’s semi-annual release cycle: assess release notes, lead sandbox testing, deploy to production with rigorous change controls

AI & Agentic Integration

  • Own the engineering of Airbnb’s Workday MCP server and its tool surface: tool design, per-user OAuth 2.0 authorization, human-in-the-loop gates on write actions, idempotent write contracts, rate and volume guardrails, and audit logging
  • Design and build agentic integrations that let AI assistant plugins and other enterprise LLM tooling read from and act on Workday safely, with permissions resolved as the authenticated user and no shared service-account fallback for user-attributable actions
  • Co-own the Talent Systems AI architecture and governance framework with the Systems Architect: how agentic tools, Workday-native AI, and enterprise LLM capabilities interconnect, and the guardrails that govern their adoption
  • Evaluate Workday-native agentic capabilities (Agent Ready Tools, MCP Explorer, Workday Agents) and emerging HR AI platforms; provide structured build-vs-buy-vs-configure analysis
  • Translate business use cases into AI tool architectures that are operationally feasible, permission-safe, and measurable
  • Instrument AI tooling for usage and cost (per-tool call metrics) to inform Workday platform entitlement and licensing decisions

Production Reliability, Security & Platform Governance

  • Drive operational excellence across the integration portfolio: SLAs, prioritization, and escalation handling
  • Own SLAs for the most critical integrations and AI tools; establish monitoring, alerting, reconciliation, and runbook standards that raise the bar across the team
  • Drive root cause analysis on integration failures and implement preventative controls
  • Own security, compliance, and governance from the integration and engineering perspective: PII handling, audit controls, and data reconciliation strategies that meet GDPR, SOC 2, SOX, and applicable data privacy requirements for HR data flows
  • Enforce authentication and transport security across all integration surfaces: OAuth 2.0 (including user-context flows), SAML, and secure file transfer (PGP, SFTP)
  • Assess system impacts and risks when introducing new integrations, AI tools, or platform changes, and communicate them clearly before promotion to production
  • Own tenant deployment strategy: sandbox-to-production promotion, Git-based version control of integration and Extend artifacts, CI-friendly testing, and rollback planning

HR Technology & Functional Fluency

  • Maintain a strong working understanding of core HR and payroll processes (hire-to-retire, compensation cycles, benefits enrollment, time and absence, compliance reporting) sufficient to design integrations and AI tools that reflect real business requirements
  • Understand how HR data flows across the enterprise: from Workday as the system of record through downstream payroll processors, benefits carriers, identity providers, and compliance platforms
  • Proactively surface configuration and upstream data issues that affect integration reliability, and partner with the Systems Architect and functional owners to resolve them
  • Bring an employee-centric lens to integration and AI tool design so the technology we build translates to seamless experiences for the people it serves

Technical Leadership & Cross-Functional Influence

  • Act as the technical authority for Workday integrations and HR agentic tooling across BizTech; influence architectural decisions in adjacent teams including Enterprise Integrations, Identity, Data Platform, and AI Products
  • Mentor and upskill senior and mid-level engineers through design reviews, code reviews, pair development, and documented standards
  • Partner with Employee Experience, Recruiting, Payroll, Total Rewards, Legal/Privacy, IT Security, and enterprise architecture to translate ambiguous requirements into sound technical architectures; communicate constraints, trade-offs, and risks at all levels
  • Write authoritative Integration Design Documents, MCP tool specifications, and operational runbooks maintainable by the broader team
  • Proactively identify systemic risks and portfolio health issues; drive resolution and communicate transparently with leadership
  • Represent Talent Systems in enterprise architecture forums, AI tooling quality reviews, and vendor technical discussions; maintain active knowledge of the Workday roadmap and HR technology trends

Your Expertise

Required

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent experience)
  • 9+ years of experience in enterprise technology, software development, or systems integration, with at least 5–6 years of hands-on Workday integration development covering the full lifecycle: requirements, design, build, testing, go-live, and post-production support
  • Workday Integration Proficiency (personally written code required):
    • Workday Studio: complex multi-step integrations, sub-integrations, custom error handling and fault frameworks, XSLT transformations
    • Core Connectors and EIBs: worker data, business process events, payroll and benefits outbound connectors; clear judgment on EIB use cases and limitations versus Studio; Document Transform payload mapping
    • Payroll interfaces: PECI and PICOF, and their interaction with third-party payroll providers
    • RaaS (Report-as-a-Service): advanced report design, calculated fields, and API endpoint exposure
    • Workday Web Services (WWS): WSDL reading, SOAP/REST calls, versioning, and error response handling
  • Workday-Native & Functional Fluency:
    • Expert proficiency in XSLT, XML, and JSON; comfortable with Java sufficient for Workday Studio custom steps
    • Working knowledge of the Business Process Framework and how events trigger integration flows
    • Familiarity with Workday functional configuration across HCM, Benefits, Payroll, Security, and Time & Absence, sufficient to independently diagnose upstream data and process issues (deep functional configuration expertise is not required)
    • Foundational understanding of HR and payroll processes and how they generate the data that integrations carry
  • Modern Engineering & AI:
    • REST API design and OAuth 2.0, including user-context (authorization code) flows and token lifecycle handling
    • Experience building or integrating LLM-based tools, AI agents, or MCP servers with enterprise business systems, including permission-safe access patterns and human-in-the-loop controls
    • Experience integrating Workday with middleware or iPaaS platforms (MuleSoft, Boomi, Workato) and the judgment to know when middleware fits versus Workday-native integration
    • Git-based version control and structured deployment and change management practices
  • Security, Compliance & Engineering Practices:
    • Strong knowledge of data security for HR data: OAuth 2.0, SAML, secure file transfer (PGP, SFTP), PII handling, and audit requirements
    • Proven experience managing integrations across Workday’s semi-annual release cycle, including impact assessment and sandbox testing
    • Demonstrated record as a technical leader who has shaped architecture decisions and raised engineering quality across a team
    • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills; able to write clear design documents and runbooks, and present technical trade-offs to non-technical stakeholders
    • Ability to operate effectively in unstructured, fast-moving environments and drive toward outcomes under ambiguity
    • Experience working in an Agile/Scrum environment

Preferred

  • Workday Pro Certification in Integrations (highly valued)
  • Hands-on experience with Workday Extend (data models, UI pages, Extend REST APIs, orchestrations); accelerates ramp into Extend build work
  • Workday Pro Certification in Extend
  • Hands-on experience with Workday Orchestrate
  • Proficiency in TypeScript/Node and Python for services, tooling, and test harnesses outside the Workday tenant
  • Familiarity with Workday’s native agentic capabilities (Agent Ready Tools, MCP Explorer, Workday Agents) and their trade-offs versus custom MCP tooling
  • Experience shipping LLM plugins or agents to an enterprise employee population, including evaluation and quality review
  • Experience supporting global, multi-country HR technology environments
  • Knowledge of GDPR, India DPDP, SOC 2, or SOX requirements in the context of HR data flows
  • SQL and data-warehouse fluency for reconciliation, analytics, and People Analytics partnership

title: Senior Software Engineer, Custody Services
description:
Join us in building the future of finance.

Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading.

About the team + role

We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world’s biggest financial problems. We’re looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards.

The Custody Services team is responsible for managing our crypto infrastructure, digital asset custody providers, and the various integrations we maintain with third-parties — from wallet management to crypto infrastructure management! The team is also responsible for processing crypto transactions, as well as products like staking, lending, and travel rule compliance. We currently safeguard billions in assets under custody for millions of customers.

As a Senior Backend Engineer on this team, you'll work on the infrastructure behind crypto processing, wallet and key management workflows, and our integrations with third-party custodians. Most of what you'll build sits at the boundary between infrastructure and security.

This role is based in our London, UK office(s), with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week. At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams.

Requires participation in an on-call rotation to support business needs.

What you’ll do

  • Build and run the AWS infrastructure behind custody, key management, and blockchain node operations.

  • Automate infrastructure and configuration management (Ansible, Terraform, or similar) so the team spends less time on manual operations.

  • Run our blockchain nodes across the networks we support, and keep them healthy and available.

  • Write and maintain services in Python for infrastructure management and wallet operations.

  • Own the integrations with third-party custodians.

  • Build out Kubernetes and Docker deployments as we containerize more of the custody stack.

  • Set up monitoring and alerting (Prometheus, Grafana, or equivalent) so we know about problems before customers do.

  • Apply security controls and standards throughout — access control, key management, incident response.

  • Provide on-call support, responding to and resolving production issues to keep custody systems reliable and available.

What you bring

  • Senior-level experience running cloud infrastructure (AWS) in production.

  • Experience managing blockchain nodes in production.

  • Hands-on experience with Ansible, Terraform, or similar configuration management and Infrastructure as Code tooling.

  • Experience running containerized workloads on Kubernetes and Docker.

  • Solid Python and/or Go skills, with real production experience.

  • A strong security focus — you've worked on systems where key management and access control are critical.

  • Experience with Prometheus, Grafana, or an equivalent monitoring stack.

Bonus points

  • Experience integrating with third-party custodians like BitGo or Fireblocks — this is a key differentiator for this role.

What we offer

  • Challenging, high-impact work to grow your career

  • Performance driven compensation with multipliers for outsized impact, bonus programs, and equity ownership

  • Top tier benefits to fuel your work, including supplemental health insurance, ancillary insurance, and mental health support programs

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is organized around the north star goal of building an AI scientist – a system capable of solving the long term reasoning challenges and basic capabilities necessary to push the scientific frontier.

About the role

As a Research Engineer on our team you will work end to end across the whole model stack, identifying and addressing key infra blockers on the path to scientific AGI. Strong candidates should have familiarity with elements of language model training, evaluation, and inference and eagerness to quickly dive and get up to speed in areas they are not yet an expert on. This may include performance optimization, distributed systems, VM/sandboxing/container deployment, and large scale data pipelines. Join us in our mission to develop advanced AI systems pushing the frontiers of science and benefiting humanity.

  • Design and implement large-scale infrastructure systems to support AI scientist training, evaluation, and deployment across distributed environments
  • Identify and resolve infrastructure bottlenecks impeding progress toward scientific capabilities
  • Develop robust and reliable evaluation frameworks for measuring progress towards scientific AGI.
  • Build scalable and performant VM/sandboxing/container architectures to safely execute long-horizon AI tasks and scientific workflows
  • Collaborate to translate experimental requirements into production-ready infrastructure
  • Develop large scale data pipelines to handle advanced language model training requirements
  • Optimize large scale training and inference pipelines for stable and efficient reinforcement learning

  • Have 6+ years of highly-relevant experience in infrastructure engineering with demonstrated expertise in large-scale distributed systems
  • Are a strong communicator and enjoy working collaboratively
  • Possess deep knowledge of performance optimization techniques and system architectures for high-throughput ML workloads
  • Have experience with containerization technologies (Docker, Kubernetes) and orchestration at scale
  • Have proven track record of building large-scale data pipelines and distributed storage systems
  • Excel at diagnosing and resolving complex infrastructure challenges in production environments
  • Can work effectively across the full ML stack from data pipelines to performance optimization
  • Have experience collaborating with other researchers to scale experimental ideas
  • Thrive in fast-paced environments and can rapidly iterate from experimentation to production

Strong candidates may also have:

  • Experience with language model training infrastructure and distributed ML frameworks (PyTorch, JAX, etc.)
  • Background in building infrastructure for AI research labs or large-scale ML organizations
  • Knowledge of GPU/TPU architectures and language model inference optimization
  • Experience with cloud platforms (AWS, GCP) at enterprise scale
  • Familiarity with VM and container orchestration.
  • Experience with workflow orchestration tools and experiment management systems
  • History working with large scale reinforcement learning
  • Comfort with large scale data pipelines (Beam, Spark, Dask, …)

title: Capacity Planning Engineer
description:
About Us

At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.

At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.

Available Locations: Austin, Texas

About the role

The Demand Planning team sits at the intersection of traffic forecasting, infrastructure strategy, and operational execution. We predict when, where, and how many servers to deploy across Cloudflare's global edge so that customers' traffic stays in-region and they never have to think about infrastructure. This is not a reporting role — it is a planning and engineering role that requires you to build the models, own the data, and translate forecasts into real deployment decisions.

As a Capacity Engineer, you will own one or more planning regions end-to-end with light supervision. That means maintaining the models, catching problems before they become incidents, working directly with hardware sourcing and infrastructure teams, and contributing to the data pipelines that feed your planning work. You will be the point of contact for your region — not someone who supports a more senior planner, but someone who runs the work.

This is a role for someone with 3-5 years of experience who is ready to operate with real ownership and is actively growing toward full autonomy. You will work alongside senior peers who set team-wide standards, and you will be expected to contribute to cross-regional consistency — not just execute within your own lane. You will also work fluently with AI tooling, including OpenCode AI and MAS agent workflows, as a normal part of how planning gets done on this team.

Why Cloudflare/ Why This Team

Cloudflare's network spans hundreds of cities and carries a meaningful fraction of global internet traffic — the planning decisions this team makes have direct consequences at that scale. The Demand Planning team is in an active transition from manual planning toward intelligent, automated, AI-augmented capacity systems, and this role puts you at the center of that shift. You will work on problems that are genuinely hard, with teammates who take the craft seriously, in a team small enough that your work is visible and your contributions matter from day one.

What you'll do

- Own one or more edge planning regions end-to-end, producing deployment recommendations with minimal supervision

- Maintain and continuously improve regional planning models, incorporating new traffic patterns, hardware generations, and infrastructure changes

- Build and maintain data pipelines that feed regional planning — using BigQuery, Python, and Jupyter notebooks to query, explore, and validate planning data

- Work directly with hardware sourcing, DCS, and infrastructure teams to translate forecasts into actionable deployment plans

- Proactively identify capacity risks in your region and surface them before they require escalation

- Use OpenCode AI and MAS agent tooling as a standard part of your daily planning workflow

- Contribute to cross-regional consistency efforts alongside peers — shared methodology, shared standards

- Participate in planning reviews and communicate forecast outputs clearly to non-technical stakeholders

Desirable Skills, Knowledge, and Experience:

- 3-5 years in an analytical, planning, or technical infrastructure role

- Working SQL proficiency — comfortable querying and joining datasets in BigQuery to answer planning questions

- Python proficiency — data analysis, scripting, and automation of planning workflows; comfortable working in Jupyter notebooks as a day-to-day analysis environment

- Comfort working with large infrastructure datasets and translating them into decisions

- Clear written and verbal communication — you can explain a capacity recommendation to a finance partner or a network engineer without losing either of them

- Demonstrated ability to own a workstream end-to-end with light supervision

What Makes Cloudflare Special?

We’re not just a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company. We’re a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company with a soul. Fundamental to our mission to help build a better Internet is protecting the free and open Internet.

Project Galileo: Since 2014, we've equipped more than 2,400 journalism and civil society organizations in 111 countries with powerful tools to defend themselves against attacks that would otherwise censor their work, technology already used by Cloudflare’s enterprise customers--at no cost.

Athenian Project: In 2017, we created the Athenian Project to ensure that state and local governments have the highest level of protection and reliability for free, so that their constituents have access to election information and voter registration. Since the project, we've provided services to more than 425 local government election websites in 33 states.

1.1.1.1: We released1.1.1.1 to help fix the foundation of the Internet by building a faster, more secure and privacy-centric public DNS resolver. This is available publicly for everyone to use - it is the first consumer-focused service Cloudflare has ever released. Here’s the deal - we don’t store client IP addresses never, ever. We will continue to abide by our privacy commitment and ensure that no user data is sold to advertisers or used to target consumers.

Sound like something you’d like to be a part of? We’d love to hear from you!

This position may require access to information protected under U.S. export control laws, including the U.S. Export Administration Regulations. Please note that any offer of employment may be conditioned on your authorization to receive software or technology controlled under these U.S. export laws without sponsorship for an export license.

We're looking for Data Center Engineers to be the hands, eyes and judgment on the ground at our new sites. You'll work on-site every day at your home data center, helping bring it online and keeping its hardware healthy once it's in production.

Experienced engineers will have room to act as the technical lead for their site, mentor others, and help set the standards the team uses everywhere.

When something breaks, we expect you to fix it for good, not just for today, and to use AI and automation to make the fix stick, whether that means a better runbook, a script, or a change to how the team works.

  • Verify integrator and contractor work against build specifications, drive defects to resolution, and make sure sites are production-ready before handoff.

Break/Fix and Troubleshooting

  • Triage and troubleshoot server hardware using BMC/IPMI, hardware logs, diagnostics and firmware tools. Find the root cause instead of swapping parts until something works.
  • Replace components and whole systems, including servers, switches and optics, safely and with minimal disruption.
  • Troubleshoot Layer 1 and Layer 2 issues: console into network devices, read interface and link state from the command line, inspect and clean optics, check light levels, and test fiber with a light meter or OTDR.

On-Call and Incidents

  • Take part in an on-call rotation and respond on site to incidents affecting hardware at your data center.
  • Document what happened and what you did, and contribute to root-cause analysis and follow-up actions.

AI, Automation and Continuous Improvement

  • Solve problems for good. When an issue repeats, find the underlying cause and change the process, runbook or tooling so it doesn't come back.
  • Use AI tools as part of your daily work: to speed up troubleshooting, interpret hardware and network logs, draft and improve documentation and runbooks, and summarize incidents.
  • Find repetitive manual work and remove it with scripting, automation or AI-assisted workflows, or turn it into clear requirements for tooling teams.
  • Share what works so the rest of the team can adopt it across every site.

Documentation and DCIM

  • Keep DCIM records accurate in real time, including rack elevations, cabling, power and asset location, from receipt through decommissioning.
  • Follow and improve runbooks and build standards so work is repeatable across sites.

Logistics and Hardware Lifecycle

  • Own receiving, shipping and spares inventory at your site, and process RMAs end to end.
  • Perform on-site decommissioning: unracking, serial number verification and chain of custody through handoff for secure destruction.

Vendors, Partners and Compliance

  • Escort and supervise colocation remote-hands staff, contractors and integrators working at your site, and hold them to our quality and safety standards.
  • Work directly with partner teams to coordinate access, maintenance and escalations for your site.
  • Follow physical security, access control and compliance procedures without exception, and help produce accurate evidence for audits.

Supporting Other Sites

  • Support other sites remotely, for example by guiding remote hands or reviewing documentation, and travel occasionally to help with builds or surges.

Who You Are

Careful and precise. Clean cabling, correct labels and accurate records matter to you. If it isn't documented, it isn't done.

Dependable on your own. You're often the only Cloudflare person on site. You work independently, communicate clearly with a remote team, and know when to escalate.

Security-minded. You understand that access rules and chain of custody exist for a reason, and you follow them every time.

A troubleshooter, not a parts swapper. You want to know why something failed, and you use logs, diagnostics and the command line to find out.

Someone who makes the team better. You share what you learn, help newer teammates get up to speed, and take ownership of your site's outcomes.

AI-fluent and automation-first. Your first instinct is to solve a problem for good, not work around it again. You reach for AI tools and automation to troubleshoot faster, document better and improve how the team works, and you check the output before you trust it.

Required Experience

  • Hands-on experience in data center, network or server hardware operations, including working independently on site.
  • Experience racking, stacking and cabling servers and network equipment, and replacing whole systems and components.
  • Solid working knowledge of structured cabling standards, fiber and copper, and optics.
  • Hardware troubleshooting beyond parts swaps, including BMC/IPMI, hardware logs, diagnostics and firmware.
  • Comfort with the Linux command line and with network device CLIs to troubleshoot Layer 1 and Layer 2 issues.
  • Experience with fiber inspection, cleaning and testing, including light meters or OTDR.
  • Regular, hands-on use of AI tools in your technical work, such as troubleshooting, log analysis or documentation, and examples of improving a process instead of repeating a workaround.
  • Experience with asset tracking, DCIM or inventory systems, and with receiving, shipping and RMA processes.
  • Experience working in colocation facilities and with third-party vendors or contractors.
  • Willingness to take part in an on-call rotation and respond on site.
  • Clear written and verbal communication, including documenting work and updating tickets.
  • A valid driver's license, reliable transportation, and proximity to your assigned data center.
  • Ability to travel occasionally to other sites.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience as a technical lead or primary on-site contact for a data center, including leading on-site incident response.
  • Experience mentoring or training other technicians or engineers.
  • Experience writing runbooks, build standards or checklists used across multiple sites.
  • Experience supporting or leading new data center builds or integrated rack deployments.
  • Scripting experience (for example Bash or Python), or experience building automation or AI-assisted workflows that reduced manual work.
  • Certifications such as CompTIA A+, Network+ or Linux+, CCNA, BICSI, or data center certifications (for example CDCP or CDCTP).
  • Experience with DCIM and source-of-truth tooling such as NetBox or Nlyte, and Jira-based workflows.
  • Experience at a hyperscaler, cloud provider, major CDN or similarly large infrastructure operator.
  • Experience with ITAD and secure destruction processes.

We also consider candidates earlier in their careers who bring strong fundamentals and a drive to learn.

Deliver tailored technical presentations, architectural diagrams, and demonstrations that show how Cloudflare solves specific performance, security, and reliability challenges. Proactively address complex technical objections, security compliance questions, and edge-case architectural requirements during the sales cycle. Take accountability for a suitable solution deployment strategy (Customer, Partner or Cloudflare Professional services) being an integral part of all proposals.
  • Customer Adoption & Value Realization: Provide oversight to technical onboarding and implementation, but not execute the implementation, serving as the primary executive and engineering contact for the customer. Design structured migration and onboarding blueprints tailored to the customer’s environment (e.g. DNS migrations, Zero Trust rollouts, WAF tuning guidance), and act as the lead consultant for customer engineering teams, walking them step-by-step through configuration best practices. Partner with Account Executives to own discovery, demos, onboarding, technical health, risk, and expansion strategy. Proactively monitor customer health scores and telemetry to ensure rapid time-to-value, resolve integration bottlenecks, and reduce deployment risk.
  • Commercial Accountability & Expansion: Carry a variable quota tied directly to new business acquisition and/or ongoing account growth. Be commercially accountable for ensuring deep platform adoption, retaining revenue, and identifying strategic cross-sell and up-sell opportunities based on product usage data. Lead technical Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) to translate platform capabilities into return on investment for C-level executives.
  • Trusted Advisory: Act as a trusted technical advisor throughout the entire customer lifecycle, maintaining a continuous, deep relationship with key stakeholders from initial onboarding through maturity, renewal, and expansion. Provide thought partnership on architecture, AI control layers, security posture, and deployment confidence. Identify potential deployment risks or integration bottlenecks early, and provide remediation strategies to de-risk customer outcomes.
  • AI Orchestration & Workflow Automation: Leverage AI agents, Large Language Models (LLMs), and internal platforms to automate routine tasks such as RFP/Security Questionnaire responses, sandbox provisioning, basic telemetry monitoring, and internal/external documentation, reclaiming your time for strategic customer advisory.
  • Education & Enablement: Partner closely with the Enablement Team to design, build, and govern technical resources. Define, document, and educate both internal teams and customers on deliverables such as Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), architectural best practices, and technical guides to continuously raise the technical baseline across the organization.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Experience: Experience in a customer-facing technical role, such as Solutions Engineering, Customer Engineering, Professional Services, Sales Engineering, Technical Account Management, or as a Forward Deployed Engineer (years of experience required will vary based on Associate, Senior, Staff, or Principal leveling).
  • Architectural Mindset: Ability to white-board, design, and articulate complex enterprise network and security architectures clearly.
  • Consultative & Advisory Skills: Excellent communication skills with the ability to translate deeply technical concepts into business outcomes for both hands-on engineers and C-level executives.
  • Commercial Mindset: Proven track record of operating in a quota-carrying or revenue-aligned environment, with a strong understanding of SaaS metrics, business value translation, and enterprise sales cycles.
  • Communication: Exceptional presentation and stakeholder management skills, capable of bridging the gap between deep technical implementation details and high-level C-suite business strategy.
  • Technical Breadth: We do not expect every candidate to be an expert in every domain. Qualified candidates will demonstrate depth in at least four of the technical areas below:
    • Internet fundamentals: Deep understanding of how the Internet works, including OSI Model layers 1–7, BGP, GRE, TCP/UDP, DNS (authoritative and recursive), HTTP(S), and SSL/TLS.
    • Security: Expertise in the security of Internet properties, including WAF, Bot Management, Firewalls, Rate Limiting, (M)TLS, Zero Trust, and SASE concepts.
    • Performance: Expertise in the performance of Internet properties, including speed, latency, caching, video streaming, HTTP/2, and TLS 1.3.
    • AI Proficiency: Familiarity with prompt engineering, AI-assisted scripting and log analysis, LLM utilization, and workflow automation to augment everyday CE workflows.
    • Coding/Scripting: Proficiency in Python, JavaScript, Bash, Lua, Go, or similar languages to write custom integration scripts, API connectors, and edge computing functions.
    • Developer Platform Fluency: Experience designing, building, deploying or scaling applications using RESTful/GraphQL APIs, SDKs, webhooks, and developer tooling in cloud-native environments. Familiarity with infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, Pulumi), CI/CD pipelines, and observability for developer-led deployments.

Strongly Preferred Qualifications (The "Good-to-Haves")

  • Technical Enablement: Track record of creating and delivering technical enablement - workshops, code samples, documentation, or developer onboarding - that accelerates customer adoption of complex platforms.
  • Applied AI Knowledge: Experience with LLM orchestration, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architectures, and model-access controls.
  • Regulatory Knowledge: Understanding of regulatory requirements such as PCI DSS, HIPAA, and SOC 2.
  • Hyperscaler / Digital Native Background: Talent coming out of hyperscalers, digital natives, distributed systems environments, or startups is strongly valued for its deeper cloud fluency and advanced architecture depth.

Education

Undergraduate or graduate degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field.

Travel

This role may require travel up to 20–50% to attend customer meetings, conferences, industry events, and in-person team collaboration.

This role features a competitive base salary and a variable compensation structure tied directly to the successful execution of full-lifecycle commercial targets, including new business acquisition, ongoing adoption milestones, and overall account expansion. Twilio is looking for a Staff Site Reliability Engineer to join our Platform Engineering organization. SRE owns production health and resiliency at Twilio — we are accountable for whether our services stay available, performant, and recoverable for the customers who build their businesses on us. SREs here are software engineers who focus on reliability: you will architect systems with reliability designed in from the outset, define the SLIs and SLOs that determine whether we are meeting customer expectations, and build the automation that keeps our infrastructure efficiently ahead of capacity and performance demand.

At the Staff SRE you work without day-to-day guidance, applying deep subject-matter knowledge and industry-leading practice to improve the products, processes, and services that Twilio runs on. You will own the reliability posture of significant parts of our production estate. Your impact will be felt across multiple teams rather than within one.

This is a hands-on engineering role. You will write and deploy code that improves service reliability, orchestrate complex changes across systems, lead the response when production is degraded, and raise the quality bar for the engineers around you.

Responsibilities

In this role, you’ll:

  • Own the reliability posture of production services in your area — availability, latency, capacity, efficiency, performance, and the monitoring and alerting that makes them visible
  • Define, instrument, and operate against SLIs and SLOs, and use error budgets to drive engineering priorities
  • Identify trends and problem areas that threaten stability, and provide a path forward to mitigate risk before it reaches customers
  • Drive down repair items and prevent classes of incidents rather than resolving them one at a time
  • Improve detection, response, and recovery — reducing time to acknowledge, engage, mitigate, and restore, with fewer people pulled in
  • Design for failure: strengthen failure domains, validate recovery paths, and make production changes safer to ship and safer to roll back
  • Participate in on-call for the services you support, and lead the response when production is degraded
  • Write post-mortems that identify true root causes, and drive the follow-up work to completion
  • Oversee efforts to identify, diagnose, report, and document production problems across all reliability dimensions
  • Write, configure, and deploy code that measurably improves service reliability — maintainable, reviewed, documented, and well tested
  • Orchestrate complex changes across systems and services, documenting design changes, technical decisions, migration plans, and upgrades
  • Lead debugging, troubleshooting, and analysis of service architecture and design
  • Use code review to drive up the quality of your coworkers' code
  • Reduce the operational overhead required to run infrastructure and services
  • Drive projects from conception to completion for efforts spanning the concerns of your team
  • Coordinate across programs, collaborating with others to estimate and communicate delivery timelines
  • Break projects into milestones and tasks, track progress, and communicate updates to stakeholders
  • Identify and communicate changes that may impact stability

Qualifications

Twilio values diverse experiences from all kinds of industries, and we encourage everyone who meets the required qualifications to apply. If your career is just starting or hasn't followed a traditional path, don't let that stop you from considering Twilio. We are always looking for people who will bring something new to the table!

*Required:

  • 8+ years of related engineering experience, with a substantial portion focused on reliability, infrastructure, or platform engineering
  • Demonstrated accountability for production systems — you have carried a pager for services that mattered and owned the outcome when they failed
  • Strong software engineering fundamentals: you build and ship production code, not only configure tooling
  • Experience defining and operating against SLIs and SLOs, and using error budgets to inform engineering priorities
  • Depth in production operations: incident command, post-mortem analysis, capacity planning, and observability
  • A record of preventing recurrence — reducing incident classes and operational toil, not just closing tickets
  • Experience driving changes that span multiple teams, and the communication skills to build alignment without formal authority
  • A track record of improving the engineers around you through code review, design feedback, and mentorship
  • Experience with large-scale distributed systems in a cloud environment

Desired:

  • Familiarity with infrastructure-as-code, container orchestration, and GitOps-style delivery
  • Experience with multi-region architecture, failure-domain design, or regional expansion work
  • Background in chaos engineering, game days, or other proactive resilience validation

Location

This role will be remote, and based in Ireland.

Travel

We prioritize connection and opportunities to build relationships with our customers and each other. For this role, you may be required to travel occasionally to participate in project or team in-person meetings.

Working at Twilio offers many benefits, including competitive pay, generous time off, ample parental and wellness leave, healthcare, a retirement savings program, and much more. Offerings vary by location.

title: Principal Software Engineer, Full Stack — Codex
description:
About the Role
We’re hiring a Principal Software Engineer to help define and build the next generation of AI-powered software development workflows.


“Full stack” in this role extends well beyond traditional frontend and backend development. You will set technical direction and lead major product initiatives spanning user interfaces, developer tooling, workflow orchestration, agent and prompt design, backend systems, and cloud infrastructure.


This is a highly product-oriented technical leadership role. You will identify the highest-leverage opportunities across the software development lifecycle, turn ambiguous user and technical problems into durable product and system strategies, and lead execution across multiple engineers and partner teams. Your work will shape both the architecture of Codex and how developers around the world design, write, review, test, and maintain software.
You will operate as a senior individual contributor: remaining deeply involved in design and implementation while raising the technical judgment, execution quality, and ambition of the broader team.


In this role, you will

  • Set the technical and product direction for significant areas of Codex, translating an evolving product vision into scalable architectures and an actionable engineering strategy.

  • Lead complex, multi-quarter initiatives spanning client applications, backend services, agent systems, cloud infrastructure, and developer tooling.

  • Design AI-powered workflows that generalize across languages, codebases, development environments, and organizations while remaining intuitive, reliable, and safe.

  • Make high-consequence architectural decisions under ambiguity, balancing rapid product learning with long-term system quality and adaptability.

  • Identify opportunities that cut across existing team or product boundaries, align stakeholders around a direction, and drive the work from exploration through launch and iteration.

  • Partner closely with product, design, research, infrastructure, security, and go-to-market teams to turn emerging model capabilities and developer needs into coherent product experiences.

  • Work directly with developers, open-source maintainers, startups, and large enterprises to uncover unmet needs and distinguish foundational opportunities from incremental improvements.

  • Establish patterns and standards for reliability, observability, performance, experimentation, and evaluation across AI-powered developer workflows.

  • Serve as a technical multiplier by reviewing critical designs, mentoring engineers, improving engineering practices, and helping the team navigate its hardest product and technical decisions.

  • Contribute directly to implementation, particularly where the problem is novel, technically demanding, or requires connecting multiple layers of the product.

You might thrive in this role if you

  • Have led the design and delivery of technically complex, user-facing systems with impact extending beyond a single feature or team.

  • Combine deep software-engineering expertise with exceptional product judgment and can move fluently across product interfaces, distributed systems, infrastructure, and developer tooling.

  • Have a track record of creating clarity in ambiguous problem spaces, setting a compelling technical direction, and bringing multiple teams or disciplines along with you.

  • Remain hands-on while increasing the effectiveness of other engineers through architecture, mentorship, decision-making, and technical leadership.

  • Understand modern software-development workflows deeply and can recognize where AI agents require fundamentally new interaction and system designs.

  • Have experience building or operating AI-powered products and understand the challenges created by nondeterminism, evaluation, latency, reliability, safety, and rapidly evolving model capabilities.

  • Make thoughtful tradeoffs between speed, product learning, technical quality, and long-term leverage.

  • Develop strong perspectives from user evidence while remaining willing to revise those perspectives as technology and user behavior evolve.

  • Communicate clearly across engineering, product, design, research, and executive audiences, especially when decisions involve substantial uncertainty or organizational complexity.

  • Are energized by defining a problem as much as solving it—and by creating the technical and organizational conditions for others to deliver excellent work.

We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products.
